nodes.label: Bunny Stream Streaming Service Project Context
nodes.rationale: Session-context document for a subscription video service for the Uzbek market where video lives in Bunny Stream and the backend only verifies rights and issues a temporary signed link.

nodes.label: Server Is a Turnstile, Not a Pipe
nodes.rationale: Not a single byte of video passes through the VPS: upload goes straight from the admin panel to Bunny, playback straight from Bunny CDN to the device, and the backend only decides who may watch.

nodes.label: Streaming Service Stack (Java 21, Gradle, Vite)
nodes.rationale: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 + PostgreSQL 16 + Flyway + Gradle Kotlin DSL, React Native/Expo mobile, React+Vite+Tailwind admin, packaged as catalog / playback / subscription / user / infrastructure modules under uz.streaming.

nodes.label: Bunny Stream (Video Library + CDN Pull Zone)
nodes.rationale: Handles transcoding into four qualities, HLS segmentation and regional replication; PostgreSQL stores metadata only and thumbnails are assembled from a URL template rather than stored.

nodes.label: Directory Token Signing (isDirectory=true)
nodes.rationale: HLS is a manifest plus hundreds of segments, so a token signed for one file opens only the manifest while every segment returns 403; the token must be signed for the directory path and is then embedded in the URL path, not the query string.

nodes.label: No IP Binding on Signed URLs
nodes.rationale: A phone switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data changes IP mid-playback and would break it; account sharing is limited by an active-session counter instead.

nodes.label: Upload Signature SHA256(libraryId+apiKey+expiration+videoId)
nodes.rationale: Lifetime of at least one hour and preferably six, because large files upload slowly.

nodes.label: Bunny Webhook (unauthenticated)
nodes.rationale: It arrives with no authorization, so VideoLibraryId must be compared against ours and the handler must always answer 200 or Bunny keeps retrying.

nodes.label: TokenSigner from the Official BunnyCDN Repository
nodes.rationale: URL-signing cryptography is not to be hand-written; the official Java class is copied into infrastructure/bunny/.

nodes.label: No PATCH, DTO-Only Responses
nodes.rationale: Only GET/POST/PUT/DELETE; partial updates go through PUT with a full body, responses are Java records, errors flow through @RestControllerAdvice in a {code, message} shape, and JPA entities never leave a controller.

nodes.label: Secrets Only via Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: BUNNY_API_KEY, BUNNY_TOKEN_KEY, the JWT secret and the DB password appear in application.yml only as placeholders; direct video file links are never handed to a client, and access rights are checked on the backend.

nodes.label: Explicit Code/Developer Split and Stop Blocks
nodes.rationale: The developer is new to video streaming, so terms are explained inline, each step is marked CODE or DEVELOPER, and work halts with a STOP block whenever a dashboard action or environment variable is required; every step ends with a concrete way to verify it.
